title: AI shopping agents are spreading, but Amazon and other big retailers are limiting or blocking them
summary: AI shopping agents that buy on a shopper's behalf are getting more attention, but access is uneven. CNBC reports that Amazon has walled off its site and that eBay, United Airlines and Kohl's limit or block what agents can do, while Walmart and Sephora have opened up and Coach and Gap allow browsing but not checkout. In a Visa test of 22 models from 12 AI labs, agents failed about 43 percent of shopping runs, often by buying a product that did not meet the request. Bain & Co. puts agent purchases at about 0.4 percent of global e-commerce transactions. Who pays for an agent's mistakes is still unsettled.
why: Some customers will start arriving through software agents, so owners who sell online should decide whether to let them check out and how to handle their mistakes.
